title: History audit and MCP parity

story.need: understand content history and perform the same safe operations through MCP
story.outcome: trust every change regardless of whether a person or agent made it

scope: Display immutable revision history and audit events
Expose block catalog, page state, revisions, and audit context through MCP
Enforce read, write, and publish scopes independently
Return actionable validation and concurrency failures
Contract-test MCP discovery and tool behavior
dataRequirements: Revision history retains actor, source, sequence, schema version, and timestamp
Audit events identify action, entity, revision, actor, source, and metadata
MCP responses serialize dates and content deterministically
permissions: History requires authenticated content read permission

acceptanceCriteria.given: a page changed through multiple transports
then: every revision is shown newest first
actor source and publication state are unambiguous

acceptanceCriteria.given: an MCP token with read scope only
acceptanceCriteria.when: the client reads and then attempts a write
then: the HTTP boundary challenges for the write scope so the client can elevate authorization

acceptanceCriteria.given: equivalent admin inline and MCP draft commands
acceptanceCriteria.when: each supplies the same valid document
then: all append the same revision representation

acceptanceCriteria.given: an MCP client discovering the server
acceptanceCriteria.when: it follows protected-resource and authorization-server metadata
then: the advertised scopes match tool enforcement
